questions.q: When does the race start, and at what time?

src.t: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.rep: The race starts on Sunday 1 November 2026 at 1:02 pm, off Saint-Malo, with 115 skippers on the start line.

questions.q: How can I watch the start, and from where?
questions.rep:
There are several ways to enjoy it:

  • on the giant screens of the fan zone, at the village;
  • live on the Route du Rhum's official YouTube channel;
  • on the official website, routedurhum.com;
  • on television, on France 3;
  • from the coast, only in the areas set aside for it: the coastline is a Natura 2000 site, and protecting it is part of the event.

questions.q: How many skippers take the start?
questions.rep: 115 skippers on a single start line, across six classes. The skippers page lets you sort them: first-timers, women, former winners, skippers from the Saint-Malo area or from Guadeloupe, international entrants.

questions.q: When is the village open, and at what times?
questions.rep:
The village is open from Tuesday 20 October to Sunday 1 November: thirteen days of celebration over 70,000 m² around the harbour basins. Exhibitors open at 10 am (at noon on the first day). In the evening, a small part of the village stays open late for partying, until 1 am:

  • Tuesday 20 October: exhibitors from noon to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Wednesday 21 and Thursday 22: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Friday 23 and Saturday 24: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
  • Sunday 25 to Thursday 29: exhibitors from 10 am to 8 pm, late night from 8 pm to 1 am
  • Friday 30 and Saturday 31: exhibitors from 10 am to 10 pm, late night from 10 pm to 1 am
  • Sunday 1 November, race start day: from 10 am to 5 pm

questions.q: Is entry free? Do I need a ticket or a pass?
questions.rep:
Yes, entry is 100% free, with no ticket: no pass or booking needed, and the village is open to everyone.

There will be systematic bag checks at the entrance.

questions.q: Can I see the boats and go on the pontoons?
questions.rep:
The boats of all six classes are moored in the basins, at the heart of the village, class by class. The interactive map shows where each of them is, pontoon by pontoon.

For safety reasons, access to the pontoons is restricted to accredited people. The public can still win a few accreditations by taking part in the many competitions run on the race's social media.

questions.q: What is there to see and do at the village?
questions.rep: The whole fleet in the basins, two stages (Saint-Vincent and the Écluse stands), a big wheel, a zip line, the Art Explora museum boat and food areas. Every event, day by day, is on the Programme page; the interactive map shows every venue and every entrance.

questions.q: Where can I find the village map and the programme?
questions.rep: The village map can be downloaded as a PDF from the village page. Its interactive version, with the entrances, events and boats, is the interactive map. Every event, day by day, is on the Programme page.

questions.q: How do I get to the village without a car?
questions.rep:
By bus, Saint-Malo's network costs €1.40 online or at a sales point, €2 on board. By bike, secure bike parks are waiting at every entrance to the village, and shared e-bikes are available all over town.

The page has a tool that finds your best route depending on the region you are coming from.

questions.q: Where can I park, and is parking paid?
questions.rep: Traffic is restricted during the event, car parks are not right next to the entrances, and public parking is paid. The 2026 traffic plan, prices, charging points and closed streets are all on the page.

questions.q: Is the village accessible to people with disabilities?
questions.rep: Yes: the whole village is accessible to people with reduced mobility and people with disabilities, with dedicated arrangements: special shuttles to and from car parks, and reserved parking spaces. Dedicated priority lanes will be available at every entrance.

questions.q: Are there specific arrangements for people with disabilities?
questions.rep:
• Quiet spaces, at the heart of the village, for people with disabilities or who are sensitive to noise.
  • A quiet hour, every day from 21 to 31 October from 12:30 to 1:30 pm: a calmer time at the village, with less noise and stimulation.
  • Many talks on the village's main stage are interpreted into French Sign Language (LSF).

questions.q: Are dogs allowed at the village?
questions.rep: We love our four-legged friends 🐾, but for everyone's safety and comfort, dogs are not allowed at the village. Only assistance dogs accompanying a person with a disability are permitted.

questions.q: Can I bring a pushchair?
questions.rep: Yes, pushchairs can get everywhere in the village.

questions.q: Why the emphasis on public transport and cycling?
questions.rep: Because 64.4% of the event's emissions come from spectators travelling to the start village (ADEME figures, one way). Train, bus, bike or car sharing are the most direct way to lighten the race's footprint.

questions.q: Where can I find the GPS positions of the boats?
questions.rep:
The ranking of every position report can be downloaded as a simplified CSV file, updated continuously, with the latitude and longitude of each boat (in degrees and minutes, and in decimal), its distance to the finish, its speed and its heading. Two versions are available.

  • The spreadsheet CSV, to open in Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets.
  • The CSV for a map, to import into uMap or Google My Maps.

The full official ranking data, in XML format, is available at the bottom of the Ranking page.

questions.q: What is the Route du Rhum course?

src.t: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.rep: A solo transatlantic race from Saint-Malo to Pointe-à-Pitre: about 3,542 nautical miles, or 6,560 km. The fleet crosses the Channel, rounds Ushant, heads down into the Bay of Biscay, plays with the Azores high and then picks up the trade winds. A lap of Guadeloupe from the north is compulsory before the finish.

questions.q: What kinds of boats take part?
questions.rep: Six classes start together: Ultim, Ocean Fifty, IMOCA, Class40, and two new classes in 2026, Vintage Mono and Vintage Multi, which replace the former Rhum categories and bring legendary boats back to sea.

questions.q: How long does the race last, and what is the record?

src.t: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.rep: The record belongs to Charles Caudrelier, winner in 2022: 6 days 19 hours 47 minutes and 25 seconds aboard the Ultim Maxi Edmond de Rothschild. The smallest boats take several weeks: the fleet arrives in Guadeloupe in stages.

questions.q: Why does the race take place every four years?

src.t: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.rep: Created in 1978 by Michel Etevenon, the Route du Rhum is sailed every four years: that is how long skippers need to put a project together, and what makes each edition a rare event.

questions.q: Do professionals and amateurs really start together?

src.t: What is the Route du Rhum?

questions.rep: Yes. The race brings together professionals and amateurs, women and men, on the same start line, something rare in top-level sport. In 2022, 138 skippers started and 103 made it to Pointe-à-Pitre.

questions.q: Can I enter the race?
questions.rep:
For 2026, it is too late: the next edition will take place in 2030.

However, another legendary race is opening its doors to the Vintage classes: The Transat CIC, formerly the English Transat and the oldest of the transatlantic races, which links Lorient to New York. Its next edition will start in 2028.

questions.q: Where and when do the boats arrive?
questions.rep: Finishes are celebrated at the Mémorial ACTe, in Pointe-à-Pitre, which has welcomed every skipper since 2018, from the first to the last. The first boats are expected from 5 November 2026.

questions.q: Are there villages in Guadeloupe?
questions.rep: Yes, three: at the Mémorial ACTe, at the Bas-du-Fort marina and in Basse-Terre, for three weeks of celebration.

questions.q: How do I get to the Mémorial ACTe?
questions.rep: The Mémorial ACTe is on rue Raspail, on the Darboussier site, in Pointe-à-Pitre. Allow 10 to 15 minutes on foot from the place de la Victoire or the port; Pôle Caraïbes airport is 7 to 8 km away, about 15 minutes by taxi.

questions.q: What is My Espace Rhum for?
questions.rep: It is your personal space: follow your favourite skippers, get personalised content, take on challenges, enter exclusive competitions and collect badges as the race unfolds.

questions.q: Who can create an account, and is it free?
questions.rep: My Espace Rhum is free and requires no purchase. Sign-up is open from age 15, younger with a parent's consent. One account per person, in your own name, with a password or your Google account.

questions.q: Who can play the games and win prizes?
questions.rep: Games with prizes (wheel, predictions…) are open to adults only. Each game has its own rules, which set its dates, conditions, the number of entries allowed and its prizes. Creating several accounts leads to exclusion.

questions.q: Why doesn't my badge or ranking update straight away?
questions.rep: Counters follow your activity as it happens, then are checked and recalculated every night: a delay of a few hours is normal. A badge you have earned is never taken away. If you have switched off activity tracking in your settings, badges and statistics no longer move.

questions.q: How do I delete my account or my data?
questions.rep: Everything is done from your Espace: download your data, erase it while keeping your account, or delete the account itself. These deletions are permanent.

questions.q: How do I apply for a press or photo accreditation?
questions.rep: Pre-applications are open, only through the official form: no application sent by email will be processed. One application per person, linked to an active media outlet or a specific editorial project; the badge is personal.

questions.q: Where can I buy the poster and official merchandise?
questions.rep: On the official shop, and from the makers of official licensed products: posters, postcards, ponchos, wooden boats… Their catalogue can be downloaded from the dedicated page.

questions.q: Where can I meet TyMAL, the mascot?
questions.rep:
TyMAL is on tour before the start, in Brittany and beyond: the tour map shows the next stops, and tells you whether TyMAL is coming near you.

During the village, TyMAL is there every day. Where to find TyMAL is shown on the interactive map.

questions.q: Is there an educational kit for schools?
questions.rep:
Yes, as a free download. Written with IFREMER scientists, it introduces the ocean, the coastline and the deep sea, for children and adults alike.

A race tracking map for children will also be available soon.

questions.q: Am I allowed to take photos at the village?
questions.rep:
Yes, you may take photos at the village, in compliance with the law, in particular image rights.

However, drones are not allowed on site, except for operators holding a specific accreditation.

questions.q: Who organises the Route du Rhum?
questions.rep:
OC Sport Pen Duick is the French subsidiary of the OC Sport group in charge of offshore racing events. Created to manage the sailing campaigns of Éric Tabarly on the one hand and Dame Ellen MacArthur on the other, iconic figures of international sport, the group faithfully carries on the spirit and values of these founding pioneers: living and sharing unique experiences with the public, athletes and partners.

Long committed to offshore racing, the group has built unique expertise in professional sailing, drawing on two skills: team management, and organising the most prestigious races (Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe, The Transat CIC, La Solitaire du Figaro Paprec, the Transat Paprec, the Arkea Ultim Challenge - Brest…). OC Sport is a company of the Advenn Group.

questions.q: Can I refuse cookies, or change my mind later?
questions.rep: Yes. Audience measurement and marketing cookies are only set with your consent, and refusing them does not stop you using the site's main features. You can change your mind at any time: manage my cookies.

questions.q: How can I see, correct or have my personal data deleted?
questions.rep: Write to rgpd@ocsport.com, the address dedicated to data protection. You can ask to see, correct, delete or retrieve your data, and withdraw your consent. If you feel your rights have not been respected, you can refer the matter to the CNIL, the French data protection authority.

questions.q: How do I unsubscribe from the Rhum Express newsletter?
questions.rep: At any time, using the link included in every issue. You do not need to subscribe to use My Espace Rhum, and the Rhum Express badge earned by subscribing stays yours.
